documentText.text: Video production, evidence-first
From raw footage to a published, reviewed short.

ShortsOS turns a client's own raw footage into a produced, human-reviewed short — and, when genuinely ready, gets it published with a captured permalink. The steps below are the shape of the pipeline; the publication step is the one we have run for real, end to end.
The pipeline
What actually happens to a client's footage
Existing footage
A client's raw footage — the material already sitting in their own storage — is the starting point. Nothing is generated from a prompt.
Inventory
Footage is technically inspected (duration, resolution, audio presence) and organized into a searchable inventory, so nothing usable gets lost in a folder.
Understanding
Each clip is analyzed for what it actually shows — the moments, not just the file names — to build a record of what evidence exists.
Evidence
Every story candidate is tied back to the specific source moments that support it, with timestamps — so a decision can be checked against the footage, not taken on faith.
Story opportunities
Candidate short-form stories are drafted from that evidence, never invented independently of it.
Human selection
A person decides which opportunity is worth producing. This is a decision checkpoint, not an automatic pipeline.
Production
The selected story is rendered into video, voiced, and captioned.
Review
A human reviews the produced short before anything goes out. Every real run to date has included this checkpoint.
Publication Proven, real run
When a client is genuinely ready, the reviewed short is published — with a captured, checkable permalink.
What's proven
The one thing we can show, not just describe
ShortsOS has completed a real end-to-end Produce → Review → Publish workflow: from source video and render, through human review, to a live Instagram Reel with a captured publication permalink.
For pilots, the workflow is operated by the ShortsOS team.
See the full proof →

documentText.text: Methodology
How the pipeline is built, internally

ShortsOS is operated, not self-directed: an agency team runs the pipeline on a client's behalf. This page describes how that pipeline is architected internally — for transparency about the mechanism, not as a menu of features available to a visitor. Most of what is described here is internal engineering: implemented and tested, but not a capability a customer can invoke directly, and not independently marketed as its own product claim.
Internal architecture
Drive import & inventory
Footage is imported from a client's own storage and organized into a technical inventory (duration, resolution, audio presence).
Media understanding
Clips are analyzed for what they show, building an evidence record used by every later stage.
Opportunity generation
Candidate short-form stories are drafted from that evidence, with the source moments cited alongside each one.
Human decision checkpoint
An operator reviews the candidate opportunities and their supporting evidence before anything is produced.
Production orchestration
The selected opportunity moves through a durable, resumable job pipeline: render, voice, caption.
Render & caption providers
Rendering and captioning are handled by third-party providers behind the pipeline; ShortsOS owns the orchestration and the content decisions, not the underlying video/caption engines.
Review
A human reviews the produced short before publication — a mandatory checkpoint, not an optional one.
Publish & permalink capture
When ready, the reviewed short is published and its permalink is captured and recorded.
What this program actually claims publicly

As of this program's most recent internal review, the underlying capability inventory behind this pipeline is tracked on a four-way scale — proven-and-public, candidate, internal-only, and blocked — and exactly one capability has cleared the bar for a public claim: the end-to-end Produce → Review → Publish workflow described on the Proof page. Everything else described on this page is internal architecture context, not an independent public claim.

documentText.text: Proof
One real, end-to-end run — not a demo

This is the one thing ShortsOS has proven end to end, for real: a single client's raw footage went through production, a human review, and publication — resulting in a live Instagram Reel with a permalink we captured. It is one documented run, not a demonstration reel and not a repeated or automated process.
The claim, exactly as ratified
ShortsOS has completed a real end-to-end Produce → Review → Publish workflow: from source video and render, through human review, to a live Instagram Reel with a captured publication permalink.
For pilots, the workflow is operated by the ShortsOS team.
What happened

Source footage was rendered into a short, reviewed by a person, and published to a real, operator-bound Instagram account. The published post's permalink was captured and stored as the durable record of that publication. Two real adapter defects were found and fixed against the live Instagram integration during this run — evidence that the run was against the real provider, not a mock.
What this is not

This is not a portfolio of many published shorts, not a rendered demo reel, and not a claim about how the finished video looks or performs. It is a record that the mechanism — from source footage to a captured, checkable publication permalink — has actually run once, for real.
Known limits
Single real run is not a load or reliability proof; discovered Instagram adapter defects were fixed reactively against that one live run, not pre-emptively.
Never claimed
The following are explicitly out of bounds for this claim, by ratified governance decision — not just informal caution:
Any claim of automatic publishing without human review — the Review step is a mandatory human checkpoint in every real run to date.
Any claim of guaranteed creative quality.
Any claim of guaranteed performance or virality for any published content.
Any claim of production-scale or repeated-volume proof beyond the one documented real run.
Any claim of universal availability — this workflow is operated by the ShortsOS team for pilots, never generally/instantly available.
Any claim that a customer can connect their own Instagram account to this workflow.
Any claim that a customer can publish directly themselves through this workflow.
Any claim that any end user can self-serve run this loop today — it is operator-run, on one bound Instagram account.
Governance record: docs/governance/publication/2026-09-13-m1-public-marketable-ratification.md (in the ShortsOS product repository).

documentText.text: FAQ
Honest answers, including the ones that are "no"
Can I connect my own Instagram account?
Not yet. The one real publish we have run used a single account operated by the ShortsOS team. There is no independent account connection today.
Can I publish directly myself, without going through ShortsOS?
No. Publishing happens through the ShortsOS team as part of an operated pilot, not as something a customer triggers directly.
Does ShortsOS publish automatically, without anyone reviewing it first?
No. A human reviews every produced short before it is published. That review step has been part of every real run to date, and it is not optional.
Is this available to anyone right now?
No. ShortsOS is currently operated by the team for pilots — it is not a generally or instantly available product.
Has this been done many times, or at scale?
No. What is proven is one documented, real, end-to-end run. We do not claim production-scale or repeated-volume proof beyond that.
Do you guarantee the video will be good, or that it will perform well?
No. We make no guarantee of creative quality, performance, or virality for any published content.
What exactly is proven, then?
That the full Produce → Review → Publish workflow can run for real: source footage in, a real render, a human review, and a live Instagram Reel out, with its permalink captured.
How do I actually start working with ShortsOS?
Request a pilot. The ShortsOS team will follow up directly to scope a real engagement — there is no independent signup.

documentText.text: Changelog
Governance history, not a feature list

This is process/methodology history, not a customer-facing feature list. It records how ShortsOS's own governance program decides what may be claimed publicly — not a log of shipped product features. Every entry below is a historical statement about engineering or governance work that already happened, cited by real commit and date in one of the two repositories behind this site. A historical entry about a capability that is still `candidate`, `internal_only`, or `blocked` today describes past engineering work only — never a current offer to use that capability.

ShortsOS's internal capability inventory was first classified on a four-way public/candidate/internal/blocked scale, fail-closed by default — every capability started internal-only until explicitly promoted.

Internal engineering work, prior to this site's own governance train: the content-inventory UI was given real evidence controls, capture-session identity, and a durable zero-story state — the first capability in this program to be reviewed and closed across two consecutive missions. This was engineering-only work; no public claim followed from it.

Internal engineering history: the story-opportunity generator was connected to a real production LLM caller (previously a mock), closing out WAVE-006 of the earlier "From Drive to Story" build program. This is the same opportunity-generation stage later described, in past tense, on the /how-it-works page as pipeline architecture — it remains internal-only, not independently claimed here.
Tenant-safe duplicate-clip detection fixed (FDTS-RETRIEVAL-SAFETY-V1)

A real defect — a media-probe lookup that did not scope duplicate detection by tenant — was found and fixed. Internal engineering record only; retrieval safety is not a capability marketed on this site.

documentText.text: Request a pilot
Thanks for reaching out

This page confirms what happens next — it is not a submission receipt. This site has no server or database behind it, so it has no way to confirm an email actually reached us; that confirmation lives in your own email client's sent folder, not here.
What happens next
If you emailed us from the Request a pilot page, someone from the ShortsOS team will reply directly to that email, usually within a few business days.

If you don't hear back, check your sent folder to confirm the email actually went out, and feel free to send it again — there is no automated queue or ticketing system on our side that could silently drop it, but there is also no automated acknowledgment.
